clue.text: Fine victories in dangerous waters

parts.note: fine in the sense of good, satisfactory
victories are wins

explanation.surface: Triumphs scored at sea in treacherous waters.
explanation.walkthrough: The Goodwin Sands are a notorious stretch of sandbanks off the Kent coast in the English Channel, famous for shipwrecks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Goodwin Sands off Kent are shoals that have wrecked countless ships, a byword for perilous sea.

clue.text: She had a stony look

parts.note: in Greek myth a snake-haired monster's gaze turned onlookers to stone, so her look was literally stony

explanation.surface: A woman with a cold, unfriendly expression.
explanation.definitionFit: Medusa and her sisters, the mythical monsters whose glance petrified people, bear this name.

clue.text: Died sitting on a hobby-horse

indicators.note: in a down clue 'on' places the first piece above the second

parts.note: ob. abbreviates Latin obiit, 'died', on gravestones
a sitting is a session, as of a court or parliament

explanation.surface: Someone expired while perched on a child's toy horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobby-horse is a favourite fixation one keeps returning to, an idée fixe.

clue.text: The route for arms traffic?

parts.note: arms traffic suggests gun-running, but here it means armies marching to battle along their course

explanation.surface: A question about the path used by weapons smugglers.
explanation.definitionFit: The figurative road taken by those set on hostilities, from the Native American term for a war party's trail.

clue.text: Do such people want to be poor?

definitions.text: Do such people want to be poor?

parts.words: Do such people want to be poor?
parts.note: 'want' means lack rather than desire: people in want are the poor

explanation.surface: Asking whether some people actually wish for poverty.
explanation.definitionFit: The destitute lack necessities, which is exactly what want means here.

clue.text: Principal part providing the main range

parts.note: the mass of something is its bulk or greater portion
providing in the sense of 'on condition that', which is if

explanation.surface: Something supplying the chief share of a range, perhaps of goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact group of mountains forming the central heights of a region.

clue.text: A muse has the right means to make the waters sparkle

definitions.text: means to make the waters sparkle

parts.note: Erato is the Muse of lyric and love poetry

explanation.surface: A poet's inspiration has the knack of making the sea glitter.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that pumps gas into a liquid, as in fizzy drinks or ponds, makes it bubbly.

clue.text: Norse version of a Spanish title

indicators.note: a version of the word is a different form of it, so its letters are recast

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian rendering of a Spanish form of address.
explanation.definitionFit: Señor is the Spanish equivalent of Mr or sir.

clue.text: Run away, puffed out and diseased

parts.note: to fly is to flee
blown means out of breath, puffed

explanation.surface: Someone who fled, ended up breathless and ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat infested with maggots from blowfly eggs is described as tainted and corrupt this way.

clue.text: Much sought-after area bounded by the Inner Circle

definitions.text: Much sought-after area bounded by the Inner Circle

parts.words: Much sought-after area bounded by the Inner Circle
parts.note: on a dartboard or target the central spot every player aims at sits inside the ring called the inner

explanation.surface: Prime property within an exclusive elite.
explanation.definitionFit: The centre of a target, the spot everyone aims for, is enclosed by the inner ring.

clue.text: Book circulation produces liquid assets

parts.note: to book a seat is to reserve it
currency is the state of being in circulation, as of coins or ideas

explanation.surface: A library book's lending rate supposedly generating ready money.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserve currency is money held in quantity by central banks, freely spendable and so highly liquid.

clue.text: There are bones in this, as yours could be

indicators.note: 'could be' suggests the letters of the words could become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A grim reminder that your own skeleton might end up in such a place.
explanation.definitionFit: An ossuary is a vault or urn where the skeletal remains of the dead are kept.

clue.text: Misprint; though following word for word

explanation.surface: An error in printing, even if the copy was exact.
explanation.definitionFit: A printer's typo is called a literal; a literal translation keeps strictly to the original wording.

clue.text: Merrythought for the dinner break

explanation.surface: A cheerful idea for the lunch interval.
explanation.walkthrough: Merrythought is an old name for the forked bone of a fowl; after a meal two people pull it and the one with the longer piece makes a wish, so it is 'for the dinner break'.
explanation.definitionFit: Merrythought is the old word for the forked breastbone of a bird, which diners snap after eating poultry.

clue.text: Quota of deliveries rising, give out extra money

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled

indicators.note: in a down clue 'rising' means reading the word upwards

parts.note: to give out is to emit

explanation.surface: Bowling stats going up, and a bonus paid out.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls, the bowler's quota of deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: Pay earned for hours worked beyond the normal shift is additional to the basic wage.

clue.text: Begin again, in the manner of Irene with Bosinney?

indicators.note: 'in' tells us the letters sit inside the words Irene with

explanation.surface: Asks whether Irene took up her affair with Bosinney afresh.
explanation.walkthrough: Irene and Bosinney are lovers in Galsworthy's Forsyte Saga; the novel reference is surface dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew is to resume or start over, as one renews an attempt.

clue.text: Not knowing how to scatter incense over the church

indicators.note: in a down clue 'over' puts the first piece on top of the second
scattering spreads the letters of incense about in a new order

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Ignorance of how to sprinkle incense across a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to scatter' turns INCENSE into NESCIEN, set 'over' CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nescience is a formal word for ignorance, lack of knowledge.

clue.text: Passionate love for a bird

parts.note: flaming means ardent, fiery
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Ardent affection for a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall pink wading bird of lagoons.

clue.text: Ruler probably used to get creased

explanation.surface: A ruler was presumably employed to produce the folds.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition reads cryptically: a ruler is what you would use to rule paper with straight marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper ruled with straight marks is described with this word, and a creased, wrinkled face is too.

clue.text: Odd tile shape -triangular

indicators.note: to shape is to form anew, so the letters are reformed

explanation.surface: An unusual tile with three corners.
explanation.definitionFit: Deltoid means shaped like the Greek capital delta, a triangle.

clue.text: Green salad is excellent starter to invigorate

indicators.note: a salad is a jumble of mixed ingredients, so these letters are tossed together

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A green salad makes a fine first course to pep you up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salad' mixes GREEN into ENERG; 'starter' takes the first letter of 'excellent'.
explanation.definitionFit: To invigorate someone is to fill them with vitality and get them going.

clue.text: Play the game when this is jammed, said Newbolt

definitions.text: Play the game when this is jammed, said Newbolt

parts.words: Play the game when this is jammed, said Newbolt
parts.note: Henry Newbolt's poem Vitai Lampada has the line about the machine gun jamming before the cry 'Play up! and play the game!'

explanation.surface: A poet's advice to keep sporting even when things get stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: Newbolt's patriotic Victorian poem Vitai Lampada is well known in Britain: 'The ... 's jammed and the Colonel dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: The hand-cranked multi-barrel machine gun of the nineteenth century, named after its American inventor.

clue.text: Bounder is said to be this fly

indicators.note: 'said' means the words are spoken and give a word sounding the same

parts.note: a bounder is a cad; taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone claims a rotter is a kind of insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The caddis fly is an insect whose larvae build cases of debris in streams.

clue.text: He sounds a dull, vulgar seafarer

indicators.note: 'sounds' says the word that follows is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: matt describes a dull finish without shine; low means common or coarse

explanation.surface: A sailor who comes across as boring and crude.
explanation.walkthrough: Matelot is British slang for a sailor, pronounced roughly 'mat-low'.
explanation.definitionFit: Matelot is colloquial British for a seaman, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Colouring the head of the Dean of St Paul's

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: William Inge, the 'Gloomy Dean', was Dean of St Paul's Cathedral in London

explanation.surface: Painting the top of a cathedral dean's head.
explanation.walkthrough: Dean Inge of St Paul's Cathedral was a famous early twentieth-century columnist.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight trace of colour, a tint.

clue.text: Wine container is returned with its top off

indicators.note: 'is returned' means the remaining letters are read in the opposite direction
taking the top off a word removes its first letter

parts.note: a canister is a container

explanation.surface: A bottle of wine sent back with its cap removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with its top off' drops C from CANISTER to leave ANISTER; 'is returned' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Compose again — "Trees", perhaps

indicators.note: 'perhaps' hints the letters of Trees could be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Rewriting the poem 'Trees' a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges TREES; the quotation marks suggest the poem by Joyce Kilmer.
explanation.definitionFit: To reset type or music is to compose it afresh.

clue.text: This officer has not been charged, though a defender

definitions.text: This officer has not been charged, though a defender

parts.words: This officer has not been charged, though a defender
parts.note: a sergeant or corporal holds rank without a royal commission, so has never been charged with one, yet is still a soldier defending the country

explanation.surface: A soldier who remains uncharged despite serving to protect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' suggests a criminal charge, but it means entrusted with a commission.
explanation.definitionFit: Such officers are ranks like sergeant appointed from the ranks without a formal commission.

clue.text: Go too far round Dover perhaps

indicators.note: 'perhaps' hints that the letters of Dover may be arranged otherwise

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: Travelling beyond one's destination, around the port of Dover.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo something is to take it to excess.

clue.text: Illness prevents holiday clashes

explanation.surface: Sickness spoiling a holiday where everyone goes at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Staggers is a disease of livestock causing unsteady gait; staggering holidays spaces them out so they do not overlap.
explanation.definitionFit: Staggers is a disorder of horses and cattle; to stagger leave is to arrange it at different times.
